hypotheses.title: 52-Week High Anomaly Proximity Channel (ts_scale 252d) (pv1)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Directly implements the celebrated 52-Week High Anomaly (George & Hwang 2004, Finding Alphas Chapters 18 & 21). When an equity trades near its 52-week peak (ts_scale(close, 252) -> 1.0), psychological anchoring causes investors to hesitate to bid higher, creating temporarily underpriced buying opportunities that experience persistent drift once quarterly earnings momentum confirms the breakout. Evaluating ts_scale over a 252-day annual channel yields exceptionally disciplined turnover (~10%-14%), unlocking the Tulchinsky Fitness multiplier with near-zero correlation to our approved portfolio.
confounders: Broad market cyclical tops causing broad momentum crashes
Overextended speculative bubbles without fundamental support
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if equities near 52-week highs systematically suffer mean-reversion pullbacks rather than breakout continuation.

candidates.rationale: Industry-neutral 252-day time-series scale (52-week high channel) with 5-day smoothed price reversal overlay

hypotheses.title: 60-Day Rolling Price-Volume Correlation / Flow Coherence (pv1)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Directly activates the unmined ts_corr operator from Finding Alphas (Chapter 18). Institutional accumulation produces positive price-volume coherence (prices advance on volume expansion and consolidate on volume contractions). In contrast, negative price-volume correlation indicates heavy distribution and institutional dumping. Measuring the 60-day rolling correlation (ts_corr(returns, volume, 60)) identifies equities under steady institutional accumulation. Measuring correlation over a 60-day window keeps turnover smooth and low (~12%-16%), directly driving Fitness >= 1.50.
confounders: Index arbitrage program trading skewing daily volume without directional conviction
Short squeeze spikes creating transient volume-return spikes
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha breaks down if positive price-volume correlation indicates retail FOMO top rather than institutional accumulation.

candidates.rationale: Industry-neutral 60-day rolling correlation between returns and volume with 5-day reversal overlay

hypotheses.title: 120-Day Negative Return Skewness / Anti-Lottery Anomaly (pv1)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Directly activates the unmined ts_skewness operator from Finding Alphas (Chapter 22). Retail investors overpay for equities with positive return skewness (lottery-like payoff profiles with occasional extreme positive spikes), leading to depressed subsequent returns. Conversely, equities with negative return skewness trade at an empirical risk discount and deliver superior forward risk-adjusted returns. Going long low-skewness compounders (-ts_skewness(returns, 120)) systematically harvests this tail-risk anomaly. The 120-day rolling window enforces ultra-low turnover (~8%-12%), with zero self-correlation.
confounders: Hidden left-tail disaster risk in highly leveraged equities
Regime changes from low-volatility compounding into high-volatility crashes
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha underperforms if high-skewness speculative growth equities systematically outperform disciplined low-skewness compounders.

candidates.rationale: Industry-neutral negative 120-day return skewness with 5-day smoothed reversal overlay
